registers.role: outcomes: whether a primary care provider has administered a specific vaccine included in the Childhood Vaccination Program (HPV, MMR booster) and reimbursement for a Pap smear test (cervical cancer screening)
outcomes: identification of individuals who purchased the HPV vaccine, including privately purchased vaccines

registers.name_in_paper: several administrative registers, all maintained by Statistics Denmark or the Danish Health Data Authority (not named individually)
registers.role: linkage, sample frame and controls: socioeconomic background, family linkages, maternal characteristics, birth weight, immigrant status, birth order and number of siblings

linkages: individuals linked to themselves, their parents and their siblings using the unique Danish civil registration number, irrespective of co-residence (p. 6)
focal children matched to peer siblings (older and younger, same-sex and opposite-sex) so that each sibling pair is one observation (p. 7)
a siblingship is defined as both full and half-siblings from the mother's side of the family (p. 7, footnote 25)
focal children also matched to same-sex cousins for the cousin spillover analysis (p. 13, footnote 35)

sample.universe: All girls born in Denmark in 1992-1993 and all boys born in Denmark in 2005-2006 (the cohorts straddling the two HPV program eligibility cutoffs), plus their older and younger siblings born 1985-1992, 1993-1995, 1998-2005 and 2006-2008
sample.unit_of_observation: individual (population samples); sibling pair (spillover samples); girl-week (the event study)
selection_rules: girls: born in Denmark in 1992 or 1993 and living in the country in at least one year in the period 2006 to 2012 (ensuring presence in at least one year in which the vaccine was available before the catch-up program) -> 64,796 girls
boys: born in Denmark in 2005 or 2006 and living in the country in at least one year in the period 2019 to 2021 -> 64,894 boys
older same-sex sibling pairs (girls): focal girl born 1992-1993 with a sister 1 to 7 years older born 1985-1992, full and half-sisters included -> 18,754 sibling pairs
older same-sex sibling pairs (boys): focal boy born 2005-2006 with a brother 1 to 7 years older born 1998-2005 -> 20,989 sibling pairs
opposite-sex older sibling samples: 20,089 pairs for focal girls and 19,744 pairs for focal boys
younger same-sex sibling pairs: younger sister (brother) one to three years younger born 1993-1995 (2006-2008) -> 2,978 and 3,147 sibling pairs
estimation restricted to a bandwidth of 365 days around the January 1 cutoff, with triangular kernel weights
missing birth weight and maternal characteristics imputed and flagged with indicators
sample.period: 2006-2012 for the girls' program; 2019-2021 for the boys' program; the event study covers 100 weeks around the first week of October 2008
sample.n_observations: 64,796 girls and 64,894 boys (population samples); 18,754 older-sister pairs; 20,989 older-brother pairs; 20,089 opposite-sex pairs for focal girls; 19,744 opposite-sex pairs for focal boys; 2,978 younger-sister pairs; 3,147 younger-brother pairs
sample.n_individuals: in the older-sister sibling pair sample, 16,829 focal girls and 18,150 older sisters (p. 7, footnote 19)

construction_notes: HPV vaccine take-up is defined as having received the first dose; completion of the schedule (three doses for girls, two for boys) is used as a robustness check (p. 7, footnote 21)
HPV take-up is measured prior to August 27, 2012 for girls (the start of the catch-up program) and prior to December 31, 2021 for boys (p. 7)
take-up captures both privately purchased vaccines and those administered through the Childhood Vaccination Program (p. 7)
covariates are predetermined maternal characteristics measured prior to the birth of the focal individual: measured in 1991 for focal girls and 2004 for focal boys (p. 7, footnote 24)

missing values imputed: median birth weight for missing birth weight, median maternal age for missing maternal age, zeros for maternal marital status, immigrant status, education and earnings, with indicators for imputed values (p. 8, footnote 26)
running variable: date of birth centered at the discontinuity (January 1, 1993 for girls; January 1, 2006 for boys); baseline bandwidth 365 days; triangular kernel (pp. 5-6)
standard errors clustered at the family level (Table 3 notes, p. 11)
maternal yearly earnings reported in euro; birth weight in grams; age spacing in months (Tables 1-2)
the event study observes vaccination activity at weekly level for 100 weeks around the first week of October 2008 (p. 18)
cervical cancer screening is defined from the primary care physician's reimbursement for a Pap smear test (p. 7, footnote 23)

key_assumptions.assumption: Individuals cannot precisely control the running variable (date of birth) near the discontinuity point, so eligibility is as good as randomly assigned locally; in particular date of birth is not manipulated in anticipation of program eligibility.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Date of birth is determined many years before the programs; density of month of birth plotted in Appendix Figures A.1 and A.2; Frandsen (2017) manipulation test for discrete running variables cannot reject no manipulation (p-values 0.987, 0.535, 0.873, 0.747).

key_assumptions.assumption: Near-random assignment at the cutoff: predetermined covariates are independent of eligibility (no discontinuity in predetermined sociodemographic and family characteristics at the cutoff).
key_assumptions.supported_by: Table 2 (p. 10): separate and joint (SUR) regression discontinuity estimates for predetermined covariates; only a few differences significant at 5 percent and the joint null of no differences cannot be rejected at 5 percent.

key_assumptions.assumption: Continuity at the cutoff: in the absence of the program, mean vaccine take-up would be a continuous (locally linear) function of date of birth at the discontinuity point, so the jump at the cutoff identifies the effect of eligibility.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Local linear specification with a triangular kernel and a 365-day bandwidth; robustness to kernel, bandwidth (1–24 months and the Calonico et al. (2014) data-driven bandwidth) and to a donut specification; the authors note the functional form of f(⋅) should avoid identification off functional form at the cutoff (p. 5 footnote 13).

key_assumptions.assumption: No interference across the cutoff: the behaviour of the eligible cohort does not affect the behaviour of the adjacent ineligible cohort.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors argue spillovers are limited to same-sex siblings and do not extend to cousins, and that the January 1 school cutoff means eligible and ineligible focal individuals would typically not share a classroom; they concede they cannot definitively rule it out and argue any cross-contamination makes the estimates conservative.

key_assumptions.assumption: The 365-day bandwidth around the cutoff contains comparable observations on both sides (overlap in the running variable within the estimation window), and the triangular kernel weights observations by distance to the cutoff.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Bandwidth sensitivity analysis from one to 24 months and a data-driven bandwidth (Appendix Figure A.9, Appendix Table A.5 column (7)).
